<description>
The move away from libevent introduced a small regression in this regard. In #36299, we switched the timeout to apply per socket wait, but continued on to another socket wait in case of timeout, instead of returning. See commit message for details.

In general, we also shouldn't ignore `Sock::Wait`'s errors and timeouts by silently retrying forever.

Fix these issues by returning instead when `Sock::Wait` times out or returns an error. ~~Tentative bot functional test for this in second commit that appears to be robust enough.~~
</description>

<commits>
e5d9a7e04b cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable

HTTPClient::SendRequest() waits for the socket to become writable and
went back to waiting whenever Sock::Wait() returned without SendEvent.
Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That
commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started
waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected
when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the
connection open without reading the request.

Fix this by returning a failure whenever `Sock::Wait()` timeouts or errors.
</commits>
